summary: Swap-remove of an element from a flat array of pointers. Reads the array base pointer from this+0x68 (element 26), decrements the element count at this+0x64 (element 25), copies the last element into the removed slot, updates the moved element's own index field (+4 within the pointed-to element), marks the removed element handle as invalid (-1), then calls a helper with the element handle and returns its result.

operations.description: Load v2 = this[26], the pointer to the flat array base (offset 0x68).
Compute the new element count v3 = this[25] - 1 (count field at offset 0x64).
Store the decremented count back into this[25] (offset 0x64).
Copy the last element (array[v3]) into the removed slot (array[a2[1]]) within the flat array at 0x68.
Write a2[1] into the +4 index field of the element now occupying slot a2[1], keeping the moved element's stored index in sync.
Mark the removed element handle as invalid by storing -1 into a2[1].
Call the helper sub_558B30 with *a2 as its argument and return its result. The helper address is not present in the packet callee evidence.
Return the result of the helper call.

unresolved: The helper sub_558B30 called with *a2 has no callee entry in the packet; its address and semantics are not confirmed by packet facts.
No bounds check: the removed index a2[1] is assumed valid within the current count; behavior on an out-of-range index is undefined.
Element layout is only partially known: each array entry points to a record whose second DWORD (+4) stores that record's own array index.
